# ADR-07: Separate Post-Implementation Test Creation from TDD and Regression Roles

- Status: Proposed
- Decision Date: 2026-07-12

## Decision Timestamp

Date: 2026-07-12
Repository State: `f990290`
Related Task: Add TestCreatorAgent
Known Constraints At This Time: RedAgent creates pre-implementation failing tests; RegressionTestAgent adds safety nets for changes or defects; TestCreatorAgent adds tests for existing behavior without modifying production code.

## Decision Trigger

Adding tests to already implemented behavior did not have a dedicated role distinct from TDD red-phase specification and regression protection.

## Architecture Significance

Affected Areas: Testing responsibility boundaries and construction technique.
Why This Decision Is Architecturally Significant: Agent write permissions and success conditions differ by lifecycle position.

## Decision Inputs

| Input | Classification | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| TestCreatorAgent and paired wrapper exist | FACT | `f990290` |
| Production code must not be changed by this role | CONSTRAINT | `TestCreatorAgent.agent.md` |
| Three roles improve test quality over one parameterized role | ASSUMPTION | No comparative evaluation |

## Assumptions

- Callers can distinguish existing-behavior coverage from regression and red-phase work.

## Unknowns

- Overlap and misrouting frequency among the three agents.

## Options

1. Dedicated TestCreatorAgent with explicit boundaries from RedAgent and RegressionTestAgent.
2. Extend RegressionTestAgent to cover all post-implementation tests.
3. Use one parameterized test agent for every lifecycle stage.

## Decision Matrix

| Criterion | Weight | Dedicated | Extend regression | Parameterized |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Permission clarity | 5 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| Discoverability | 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 |
| Maintenance | 3 | 2 | 4 | 5 |

## Decision

Propose Option 1. TestCreatorAgent only adds tests for established behavior and does not modify production code. RedAgent remains the TDD red phase; RegressionTestAgent remains change- or defect-focused safety-net work.

## Why Not

### Why Not Option 2
Rejected Because: It collapses general coverage and regression intent. Evidence: Current contracts define different inputs. Trade-off We Avoided: Ambiguous success criteria. Trade-off We Accepted Instead: Another agent.

### Why Not Option 3
Rejected Because: A mode flag can obscure production-code permissions and lifecycle rules. Evidence: Current contracts differ materially. Trade-off We Avoided: Mode errors. Trade-off We Accepted Instead: Routing complexity.

## Adversarial Review

### Strongest Argument Against Recommended Option
The distinction may be semantic overhead without observable quality benefit.
### Failure Scenario
The same request routes differently depending on wording and produces duplicate tests.
### Hidden Cost
Three contracts and routing rules must remain synchronized.
### Assumption Most Likely to Be Wrong
Users consistently know which lifecycle category applies.
### Condition Where Another Option Becomes Better
Option 3 becomes better if permissions and lifecycle modes are mechanically enforced.

## Reversibility

Classification: HIGH
Rollback Method: Merge responsibilities and update callers.
Migration Cost: Agent references only.
Data Migration Required: No.
Downtime Risk: None.
Lock-in: Agent taxonomy.

## Reconsideration Triggers

- Confirmed duplicate work occurs across these roles twice.
- The dispatcher cannot distinguish their inputs reliably.

## Implementation Verification

### Assumptions Verified
The dedicated contract exists at `f990290`.
### Assumptions Invalidated
None evidenced.
### Unexpected Findings
No test-generation run verifies the separation.
### Decision Still Valid
UNKNOWN

## Independent Review

### Findings
Role-specific test rules are operational consequences, not separate ADRs.
### ADR Changes Required
Resolved by recording only the lifecycle boundary decision.
### Recommendation Challenged
YES

## Timeline and Contradictions

Implemented before strict ADR at `f990290`. No Accepted ADR contradiction was found.
